clue.text: Boy eats small amount with a strong, distinctive taste

indicators.note: a boy who eats something takes it inside him, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name
a lick is a small amount, as in a lick of paint

explanation.surface: A boy tucks into a small portion of something with a powerful, unmistakable flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Food heavy with garlic has a pungent, unmistakable flavour, the strong taste the clue describes.

clue.text: Lass without love creates stir

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the girl surrounds the other piece

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A girl with no sweetheart causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'stir' is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, which this older British spelling of jail names.

clue.text: Dance music for old film part

explanation.surface: A lively tune once played over a silent movie.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scottish country dance and its tune share the name, as does a spool of film.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk Scottish country dance and its tune; also a spool holding a section of cine film.

clue.text: Financially embarrassed institute — novel changes to be brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters go within the abbreviation
changes signals that the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An institute short of money is told a novel must be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the novel's letters, and 'to be brought in' sets them inside the short form of institute; 'Financially embarrassed' is a polite euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to pay one's debts, a polite way to describe being broke.

clue.text: Display of shifting patterns in space I looked around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone peering into space sees a changing display.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube of mirrors and coloured pieces that forms changing symmetrical patterns as it turns.

clue.text: Charm evident when Mum meets Jock

parts.note: Ma is an everyday word for mother
Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: Something lucky shows up when a mother meets a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock' is British slang for a Scot, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, a figure kept to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Female's humanitarian contribution

indicators.note: the contribution of a word is a part it supplies, so the name sits within the next word

explanation.surface: A woman makes a charitable donation.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, standing for a female in crossword convention.

clue.text: Insect, one trapped in ingenious beam projected

indicators.note: trapped in means caught inside, so the first pieces go within the last

parts.note: ingenious means clever
an ant is an insect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bug and a single item are caught in a cunning projected beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam fixed at one end and jutting out unsupported, as in some bridges.

clue.text: Numbers about one fellow being upset, such sad songs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the number piece goes round the rest

parts.note: threes are numbers

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Grim figures leave a fellow upset, prompting mournful songs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'being upset' turns the one-and-fellow pair upside down, reading it backwards before 'about' wraps the numbers round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirges or laments, songs of mourning for the dead.

clue.text: Deliveries not up to date, having done this?

definitions.text: Deliveries not up to date, having done this?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so deliveries are overs
something no longer current is old

explanation.surface: A firm's deliveries are behind schedule because it has promised more goods than it holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a supplier that has sold more than it can supply ends up late with its deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling beyond available stock leaves orders unfilled, so deliveries fall behind.

clue.text: The German devours a pub meal

indicators.note: devouring takes food inside, so one piece swallows the other here

parts.note: der is the German for 'the'
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A German eats a meal in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The main evening meal is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Be a weed attending joyous occasion and leave hastily

parts.note: tare is a weed, as in the biblical wheat and tares
a treat is a delightful occasion

explanation.surface: A weed at a happy event decides to slip away quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw quickly, an idiom from troops retreating, also a military ceremony.

clue.text: It may amount to a repetition involving two identical letters

definitions.text: It may amount to a repetition involving two identical letters

indicators.note: involving means taking something inside, so the pair of letters sits within the other piece

parts.note: iteration is repetition
a doubled letter, here LL

explanation.surface: A definition of a verbal device in which the same letter is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: repeating the same initial letter is exactly what the device is.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the same opening sound or letter across words is a literary device of repetition.

clue.text: Little girl, outwardly happy and dependable

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the happy word wraps round the girl

parts.note: content means happy
sis is short for sister, a little girl

explanation.surface: A small girl who seems cheerful on the surface is also reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and unvarying, so that one can rely on it.

clue.text: Travel, look, only one mile in disturbance

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: only one says that of a doubled letter just a single copy stays, so one is dropped

parts.note: a commotion is a disturbance

explanation.surface: Travel advice: look, there is only a mile to go through the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only one' leaves COMMOTION with a single M, COMOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement from place to place, the act or power of moving.

clue.text: Australian individual's a gas

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia or Australian
an individual is one; the 's is 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone from Australia is said to be great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' looks like slang for a good laugh, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule is a gas.

clue.text: Healing continuously those people admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the two-word phrase 'on end' means without a break, as in talking for hours on end
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A patient gets steadily better while visitors are let in.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text reads 'Heating', an OCR slip for 'Healing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness is said to be improving, an idiom for getting better.

clue.text: Oriental author's divided attention

indicators.note: divided means split apart, so the author goes between the letters

parts.note: to give an ear is to give attention
Laurence Sterne is the author of Tristram Shandy; 's links

explanation.surface: A writer from the Far East has distracted attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East, a synonym for a person of Asian origin.

clue.text: Show result of injury in fast vehicle

parts.note: to sport something is to show it off
a scar is the mark left by a wound

explanation.surface: Someone displays a wound mark after a crash in a speedy car.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, powerful car built for speed and handling.

clue.text: Vegetable garden mostly associated with Devon area

parts.note: Devon lies in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: A root crop grown in a garden in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of EDEN. The SW piece comes first though the clue names it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A large yellow-fleshed root, called rutabaga in North America.

clue.text: Pretty morsel put out for wild bird

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or upset, so the letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: A tasty titbit is left out to feed a wild bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small seabird of the open ocean, traditionally said to foretell storms.

clue.text: What sounds like wee creature is a much larger one

indicators.note: sounds like marks a word judged by how it is said

parts.note: a mouse is a tiny creature; 'wee' hints at a Scots accent

explanation.surface: Something that sounds like a tiny animal is in fact a huge one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Scottish accent, cued by 'wee', mouse is said moose.
explanation.definitionFit: An elk, the largest deer, far bigger than a rodent.

clue.text: Small car continuing to burn blocks motorway

indicators.note: blocks means sits in the way, inside the road, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written MI
a fire still alight is in

explanation.surface: A small car still on fire is blocking the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A small British car of the 1960s, its name meaning tiny.

clue.text: Composer of moving mass, cold and detached

explanation.surface: A composer's music is like a floating mass of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer; the word also means an iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer; a berg is a floating mass of ice broken off a glacier.

clue.text: Our leader — or the person behind our leader

explanation.surface: A newspaper names its head and the one who writes its editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' in British papers is the editorial column; the paper's head writes or directs it, and is also the paper's own chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper leads its staff and is responsible for its leading article.

clue.text: In intervening period, an indication of my divided self?

parts.note: my refers to me, the speaker
a self divided is set against itself; anti means against
the self is me

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a pause reveals their split personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as me against me, the answer pictures a self divided in two. The held text reads 'roy', an OCR slip for 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval between two events is the time in between; 'in the meantime' means meanwhile.

clue.text: Team of two beat them, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks words that are judged by their sound

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them, so 'tan them'

explanation.surface: A pair of players beat the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two working together in harness, like a bicycle built for two.

clue.text: Gazing round lake to find bird

indicators.note: round means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: gazing means staring
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Staring across a lake to spot a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A common speckled songbird that gathers in huge flocks.
